blocking: The universal wedding-day promise centers the sofreh, making Afghan and South Asian families feel secondary despite the broader positioning.
Language support is conditional in some sections but promised outright elsewhere; parents cannot confidently tell what they will receive.

fixes.what: Replace the sofreh-specific heading with “Your ceremonies are ready. Your family is welcomed.” Present sofreh checks as an example applicable only when chosen.
fixes.why: The shared service journey should speak equally to every family the studio serves.

fixes.where: how-we-work.html — Planning, service options and parent FAQ; shared footers and panels
fixes.what: Use one consistent promise: “Written translations and spoken language support are confirmed in your proposal.” Qualify each parent-page promise with the agreed language.
fixes.why: A translated document and a planner who can speak with parents are different services.

fixes.why: The current descriptions prescribe a celebration style despite the site's promise to follow each family's practice.

fixes.where: index.html — three promises; shared How we work panels — Consultation

fixes.why: Couples should see their decision-making authority as readily as parents see respect for elders.

fixes.what: Show desktop celebration names horizontally in a compact selector above the panels, retaining the expanding image treatment.
